## Problem Statement

New users face a blank platform: the first workbench, first pipeline, and first
model deployment all start from empty forms, and time-to-first-success is
measured in days. We want a curated tutorial gallery in the Dashboard — a set
of maintained, tested tutorials (notebooks and pipelines) that users can launch
into their own project with one click. This requires product code (the gallery
and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials themselves), and
documentation — three different kinds of work with different owners and review
processes.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing the pipeline). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first pipeline, first deployment, first RAG app. Each is tested against the current release. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of Dashboard releases. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process for new tutorials. |

## Affected Components

- Dashboard
- Notebooks
- Data Science Pipelines
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- Partner- or community-contributed tutorial intake (contribution process is
  documented, but no submission tooling this release)
- Localization of tutorial content

## Open Questions

None.

# Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest

## Description

Defines the tutorial packaging format — the metadata, pinned images, and validation
manifest that make a tutorial a versioned, independently testable unit, decoupled from
Dashboard releases. This is the shared contract between the tutorial gallery (which
renders and launches tutorials) and tutorial authors (who package and validate them),
covering HLR-3 of RHAISTRAT-9019.

## Scope

- Define the tutorial packaging format covering the three constituents named in the
  strategy: tutorial metadata (describing the tutorial and its journey), pinned images
  (the workbench and pipeline images a tutorial runs against), and a validation
  manifest (how the tutorial is tested).
- Define how a packaged tutorial is versioned, so tutorial content can be updated,
  re-tested, and consumed without a Dashboard release.
- Define how the validation manifest is executed to validate a packaged tutorial
  against a given release.
- Provide a worked example of one tutorial packaged in the format, usable as the
  reference for tutorial authors and for gallery consumption.
- The format definition is reviewed with the teams that consume it (the Dashboard
  gallery team and the tutorial authoring teams).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The packaging format is documented and covers metadata, pinned images, and a
  validation manifest.
- A tutorial packaged in the format can be versioned and re-validated without a
  Dashboard release.
- The worked example package passes its own validation manifest when executed
  against the current release.
- The format definition is reviewed and accepted by the consuming teams (gallery and
  tutorial authors).

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-3 (P1): "A tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation
  manifest) is defined so tutorials are versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases." This epic delivers that format. (Epic priority is P0 by
  inheritance: this format gates all P0 work in the strategy — see the decomposition
  summary's Health Warnings.)

# Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch

## Description

Delivers the tutorial gallery in the Dashboard: a curated set of maintained, tested
tutorials that users can browse and launch into their own project with one click —
opening a workbench preloaded with the tutorial notebook, or importing the tutorial
pipeline. Covers HLR-1 of RHAISTRAT-9019.

## Scope

- A tutorial gallery section in the Dashboard that lists curated tutorials with their
  packaged metadata.
- One-click launch mechanics into the user's own project:
  - For notebook tutorials: opening a workbench with the tutorial notebook loaded.
  - For pipeline tutorials: importing the pipeline into the project.
- The gallery consumes tutorials through the tutorial packaging format (metadata,
  pinned images), so tutorial content is rendered and launched from the package and
  can be updated without a Dashboard release.
- Incidental UI touch-ups (navigation labels, empty-state text) that fall out of the
  gallery change are included here; no separate documentation work is part of this
  epic.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Given the Dashboard, when a user opens the tutorial gallery, then the curated
  tutorials are listed with their packaged metadata.
- Given a notebook tutorial in the gallery, when the user clicks launch, then a
  workbench opens in the user's project with the tutorial notebook loaded.
- Given a pipeline tutorial in the gallery, when the user clicks launch, then the
  pipeline is imported into the user's project.
- The gallery renders and launches tutorials packaged in the tutorial packaging
  format; a tutorial package can be updated without a Dashboard release and the
  gallery picks it up.
- Launch behavior is verified end-to-end against at least one packaged notebook
  tutorial and one packaged pipeline tutorial.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): "The Dashboard has a tutorial gallery from which a user can launch a
  tutorial into their project (opening a workbench with the notebook, or importing
  the pipeline)." This epic delivers the gallery and its launch mechanics.

# Curated notebook tutorials for core journeys

## Description

Authors and tests the five notebook-based curated tutorials covering the core
getting-started journeys: first workbench, data prep, first training run, first
deployment, and first RAG app. Together with the first-pipeline tutorial (authored
separately under Data Science Pipelines), this completes the six curated tutorials
required by HLR-2 of RHAISTRAT-9019.

## Scope

- Author five curated notebook tutorials, one per journey:
  1. First workbench — creating a project and starting a workbench.
  2. Data prep — loading and preparing data in a workbench.
  3. First training run — training a first model.
  4. First deployment — deploying a first model serving endpoint.
  5. First RAG app — building a first retrieval-augmented generation application.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format (metadata, pinned
  images, validation manifest) so it is versioned and testable independently of
  Dashboard releases.
- Each tutorial is tested against the current release by executing its validation
  manifest.
- Tutorials are maintained content with a consistent getting-started progression
  (the curated quality bar), not one-off snippets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- Five notebook tutorials exist covering first workbench, data prep, first training
  run, first deployment, and first RAG app.
- Each tutorial is packaged per the tutorial packaging format and can be launched
  into a workbench in the user's project.
- Each tutorial passes its validation manifest against the current release.
- Tutorial content is reviewed for technical accuracy and consistency as curated,
  maintained getting-started material.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-2 (P0): "Six curated tutorials exist covering the core journeys … Each is
  tested against the current release." This epic delivers the five notebook-journey
  tutorials; the first-pipeline tutorial is delivered by the Data Science Pipelines
  tutorial work (see the decomposition summary's HLR Traceability Matrix).

  pipeline core journey (creating and running a first data science pipeline).

  getting-started material.

  tested against the current release." This epic delivers the first-pipeline
  tutorial; the five notebook-journey tutorials are delivered by the Notebooks

# Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation

## Description

Documents the tutorial gallery for users and would-be tutorial contributors: how to
use the gallery to launch tutorials into your own project, and how to contribute new
tutorials through the packaging and validation process. Covers HLR-4 of
RHAISTRAT-9019. Documentation only — no submission tooling is built (out of scope
per the strategy).

## Scope

Content outline:

- Using the tutorial gallery:
  - What the tutorial gallery is and where to find it in the Dashboard.
  - Browsing the curated tutorials and understanding tutorial metadata.
  - Launching a notebook tutorial (opening a workbench with the notebook) and a
    pipeline tutorial (importing the pipeline) into your own project.
- Contributing new tutorials:
  - The contribution process end to end: authoring, packaging per the tutorial
    packaging format (metadata, pinned images, validation manifest), and validation
    against the current release.
  - What makes a tutorial "curated" — the maintained-content quality bar.
  - How contributed tutorials are reviewed and published to the gallery
    (the process is documented; no submission tooling this release).

## Acceptance Criteria

- Documentation topics covering tutorial gallery usage and the tutorial
  contribution process are authored and published.
- The usage documentation accurately reflects the implemented gallery launch
  behavior (workbench notebook launch and pipeline import).
- The contribution documentation accurately reflects the tutorial packaging format
  and its validation flow.
- The documentation is technically reviewed against the implemented gallery,
  tutorials, and packaging format.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-4 (P2): "Documentation covers using the gallery and the contribution process
  for new tutorials." This epic delivers that documentation. (Epic priority is P1 per
  the docs-authoring exception: strategy priority Major → P1.)

# RHAISTRAT-9019 Decomposition — Curated getting-started tutorial gallery

Strategy: RHAISTRAT-9019 (Curated getting-started tutorial gallery, priority Major).

Triage: NOT below-threshold and NOT docs-only. The strategy's own problem statement
identifies three distinct work streams with different owners and review processes —
product code (Dashboard gallery and launch mechanics), authored content (the tutorials
themselves: notebooks and pipelines), and documentation — spanning four components
(Dashboard, Notebooks, Data Science Pipelines, Documentation). The multiple-distinct-
work-streams escape condition applies, so a full multi-epic decomposition was produced.

## Epic List

| ID | Title | Type | Team | Priority |
|----|-------|------|------|----------|
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 (inherited from P1 HLR-3, see Health Warnings) |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch | Implementation | RHOAI Dashboard | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E003 | Curated notebook tutorials for core journeys | Implementation | Workbenches | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | First-pipeline tutorial | Implementation | RHOAI Pipelines | P0 |
| RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 | Tutorial gallery usage and contribution documentation | Implementation (docs-authoring) | RHAI Documentation | P1 (docs-authoring exception: strategy priority Major → P1) |

## Dependency DAG

```mermaid
graph TD
    E001["E001 Tutorial packaging format and validation manifest"] --> E002["E002 Dashboard tutorial gallery with one-click launch"]
    E001 --> E003["E003 Curated notebook tutorials for core journeys"]
    E001 --> E004["E004 First-pipeline tutorial"]
    E001 --> E005["E005 Gallery usage and contribution documentation"]
    E002 --> E005
    E003 --> E005
    E004 --> E005
```

Arrows point from dependency to dependent (`E001 --> E002` = E001 must complete
before E002 starts).

Deliberate non-edge: no dependency between the Dashboard gallery (E002) and the
tutorial content epics (E003, E004). The gallery code builds against the packaging
format (a build-against artifact); the tutorials are runtime content packaged in that
format, not artifacts the gallery code builds against. The epics run in parallel;
their coupling is enforced by acceptance criteria (the gallery is verified against
format-packaged tutorials; each tutorial is validated via its packaging manifest).

## DAG Justification

| Edge | Rule | Rationale |
|------|------|-----------|
| E001 → E002 | Rule 12/13 (build-against artifact) | The gallery code builds against the tutorial packaging format — it reads tutorial metadata and pinned images to render and launch. A format/schema is a build-against artifact (API-equivalent), not a configuration reference. |
| E001 → E003 | Rule 12 (framework → consumer) | Notebook tutorials are packaged, versioned, and validated per the format; authoring against an undefined format would duplicate and risk rework. |
| E001 → E004 | Rule 12 (framework → consumer) | The pipeline tutorial is packaged and validated per the same format. |
| E001 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | docs-authoring epic is blocked by every Implementation epic; the contribution-process docs describe the packaging format itself. |
| E002 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Usage docs describe the built gallery and launch mechanics. |
| E003 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Contribution docs describe what a curated, tested tutorial looks like. |
| E004 → E005 | Rule 11 (docs last) | Contribution docs cover pipeline tutorials as well as notebook tutorials. |

Epic boundary rationale (Step 5 rules 1-2):

- E002 vs E003/E004: different components and teams (Dashboard/RHOAI Dashboard vs
  Notebooks/Workbenches and Data Science Pipelines/RHOAI Pipelines) → separate epics.
- E001 vs E003: same component and team (Notebooks/Workbenches) but different logical
  changes and work-product types — defining a packaging/validation format vs authoring
  tutorial content — with different review criteria → separate epics.
- E003 vs E004: different components and teams (Notebooks vs Data Science Pipelines);
  the first-pipeline tutorial is authored as importable pipeline content reviewed by
  the pipelines team, a different review cycle from notebook content → separate epics.
- E005: documentation is a distinct work-product type and the strategy lists
  Documentation as an affected component → separate docs-authoring epic. Content
  authoring of the tutorials themselves is NOT folded into it — tutorials are curated
  examples, a different work stream from Red Hat docs topics.
- HLR-4 is P2 but E005 is P1 per the docs-authoring priority exception (strategy
  frontmatter priority Major → P1); docs-authoring epics do not push priority upstream.

## HLR Traceability Matrix

| HLR | Priority | Epic(s) | Notes |
|-----|----------|---------|-------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E002 | Gallery and one-click launch mechanics (workbench notebook or pipeline import). |
| HLR-2 | P0 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E003, RHAISTRAT-9019-E004 | The six curated tutorials split by component: five notebook journeys (first workbench, data prep, first training run, first deployment, first RAG app) in E003; the first-pipeline tutorial in E004. Both epics are P0; neither is deferrable — HLR-2 requires all six. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E001 | Priority raised P1 → P0 by inheritance: E001 transitively enables HLR-1 and HLR-2 (all P0 work). See Health Warnings. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | RHAISTRAT-9019-E005 | docs-authoring priority exception: strategy priority Major → P1. |

All four HLRs are covered; no orphaned requirements.

## Health Warnings

1. **Priority inversion (HLR-3, P1 → E001 P0).** The strategy labels the tutorial
   packaging format P1, but the format is a prerequisite of both P0 HLRs: the gallery
   builds against it and every tutorial is packaged and validated per it. By the
   priority-inheritance rule (an epic blocking all P0 work is implicitly P0), E001 is
   set to P0. Human verification recommended: if the strategy authors intended the
   gallery and tutorials to ship WITHOUT the independently-versioned packaging format
   (e.g. tutorials bundled with Dashboard releases as a stopgap), the E001 → E002 /
   E003 / E004 edges should be revisited and E001 returned to P1 — that is a product
   sequencing decision the strategy text does not settle.
2. **Missing strategy sections.** The strategy has no Impacted Teams table, no
   Dependencies table, no Given/When/Then acceptance criteria, and no non-functional
   requirements; Affected Components is a bare list without change/owner columns.
   Teams were taken from `.context/architecture-context/` owning teams (Dashboard →
   RHOAI Dashboard; Notebooks → Workbenches; Data Science Pipelines → RHOAI
   Pipelines). Documentation has no architecture-context file, so its team
   ("RHAI Documentation") is inferred. Epic acceptance criteria below are derived
   from HLR text rather than strategy ACs.
3. **Epic size over the ~2-week guideline (E003).** Estimate: five authored, curated,
   release-tested notebook tutorials in one epic — plausibly at or above the ~2-week
   epic guideline (the strategy provides no effort arithmetic). Kept whole because
   the five tutorials form one curated, jointly-tested content set sharing the
   packaging format, authoring workflow, and review cycle; splitting would fragment
   one content stream and duplicate the shared setup/validation work per fragment.
